title: Cloud Connector tunnels to Service Edges: primary, secondary, tertiary, fail-close and fail-open

prose.text: Each Cloud Connector keeps its own tunnels to Zscaler Service Edges; the cloud load balancer in front of it is a different layer ([[cloud-connector.overview.load-balancing]]). {{data-plane}}

prose.label: Which Service Edge.
prose.text: {{geolocation-default}} The default rule that sends internet-bound traffic to Internet & SaaS is described in [[cloud-connector.forwarding.predefined-rules]].

steps.text: {{tertiary}} Whether the tertiary attempt can be turned off or chosen is open {{gap:tertiary-control}}.

prose.text: What becomes of sessions already on the secondary when the primary returns is not stated {{gap:sessions-on-failback}}.

prose.label: When no Cloud Connector reaches a Service Edge.
prose.text: {{fail-close-default}} {{fail-open-option}} The two clauses of the fail-open description are hard to reconcile, and where the toggle lives is not named {{gap:fail-open-egress}}.

prose.label: Private Access.
prose.text: {{zpa-enrolled}} {{zpa-nearest}} That the Cloud Connector and the App Connector never connect directly is not stated {{gap:no-direct-path}}.

The console's Inactive status reflects a lost management plane while the data plane keeps forwarding: [[cloud-connector.insights.connector-status:inactive-meaning]]. Control plane health checks are among the Event log triggers: [[cloud-connector.logs.event-records:when-generated]]. The direction and ports of the control channel are not stated {{gap:control-plane}}.

checks.do: Whether any Cloud Connector in the group could reach an Internet & SaaS Service Edge; only when none could does the fail-close or fail-open setting decide the outcome.
The gateway the forwarding rule uses, and its `failClosed` value.
Whether an outage lasted less than the roughly 30 seconds the failover to the secondary tunnel takes.
For Private Access traffic, whether the Cloud Connector is enrolled with Private Access and an App Connector serves the application.

data-plane.statement: The data plane processes and forwards workload traffic to Internet & SaaS and Private Access Service Edges, and is made of outbound connections from the service interface of each Cloud Connector.

quotes: The data plane is used to process and forward workload traffic to Internet & SaaS Public Service Edges or Private Service Edges and Private Access Public Service Edges or Private Service Edges.
The data plane is composed of outbound connections from the service interface of each Cloud Connector.

geolocation-default.statement: The Internet & SaaS and Private Access Service Edges are selected using geolocation; traffic forwarding rules can instead use specific Public Service Edges, Virtual Service Edges, or sub-clouds for given Cloud Connector groups and locations.

quotes: the Internet & SaaS Public Service Edges or Private Service Edges and Private Access Public Service Edges or Private Service Edges are selected using geolocation.
It is possible to configure traffic forwarding rules to utilize specific Public Service Edges, Virtual Service Edges, or sub-clouds for various Cloud Connector groups and locations.

primary-active.statement: Workload traffic handled by rules with the Internet & SaaS forwarding method uses the primary gateway as the active tunnel to the Service Edges.

quotes: Workload traffic that is processed by traffic forwarding rules configured with the Internet & SaaS forwarding method uses the primary gateway as the active tunnel to the Internet & SaaS Public Service Edges or Private Service Edges

secondary-failover.statement: On a failed connection, Cloud Connector marks the secondary gateway as the active tunnel and forwards workload traffic through it; when the primary is healthy again it is marked active and new sessions go through the primary tunnel.

quotes: In the event of a failed connection, Cloud Connector marks the secondary gateway as the active tunnel and forwards workload traffic via the secondary gateway

When the primary gateway is healthy again, it is marked as active and Cloud Connector forwards new sessions to the Internet & SaaS Public Service Edges or Private Service Edges and Private Access Public Service Edges or Private Service Edges via the primary gateway tunnel.

failover-30s.statement: Cloud Connector monitors its gateway connections, and if the active tunnel fails it fails over to the secondary tunnel in approximately 30 seconds.

quotes: Cloud Connector monitors the gateway connections to ensure the data path exists
the Cloud Connector will fail over to the secondary tunnel in approximately 30 seconds.

tertiary.statement: By default, Cloud Connector automatically tries a tertiary Service Edge if the primary and secondary have failed; it is not limited to the two Service Edges selected for tunneling.

quotes: By default, Cloud Connector automatically tries to connect to a tertiary Internet & SaaS Public Service Edge
if the primary and secondary have failed.

Cloud Connector is not limited to just the two Internet & SaaS Public Service Edges or Private Service Edges and Private Access Public Service Edges or Private Service Edges that are selected for tunneling.

fail-close-default.statement: The default gateway configuration fails closed: internet-bound workload traffic is dropped if none of the Cloud Connectors in the same group can establish connectivity to any Internet & SaaS Service Edge.

quotes: The default gateway configuration will fail-close, meaning that internet-bound traffic from workloads is dropped if none of the Cloud Connectors in the same group are able to establish connectivity to any of the Internet & SaaS Service Edges.

fail-open-option.statement: Customers can change this to fail-open, which lets workloads accessing the internet continue to do so; the same sentence says the fail-open option means egressing traffic flows through Zscaler for inspection and policy control.

quotes: Customers can change this configuration to fail-open, allowing workloads that are accessing the internet to continue doing so. The fail-open option means the egressing traffic is flowing through Zscaler for inspection and policy control.

gateway-fail-closed-field.statement: The API's forwarding gateway object (`/gateways`) has a `failClosed` boolean: true means traffic is dropped when both the primary and secondary proxies defined in the gateway are unreachable, false means it is allowed.

expect.description: A true value indicates that traffic must be dropped when both primary and secondary proxies defined in the gateway are unreachable. A false value indicates that traffic must be allowed.

fail-closed-is-the-toggle.statement: The fail-close or fail-open choice the high-availability article describes may be this per-gateway `failClosed` setting, which would make it a property of the forwarding gateway a rule uses rather than a tenant-wide switch.
fail-closed-is-the-toggle.conditions: Inference: the help article names no setting, and the API description speaks of the gateway's primary and secondary proxies rather than of all Cloud Connectors in a group. Confirm in a tenant before relying on it.

zpa-enrolled.statement: Cloud Connectors enrolled with Private Access automatically establish a secure connection to an optimal Private Access Public or Private Service Edge; workloads reaching private applications are tunneled there, and the data path continues through the App Connectors configured for the application.

quotes: Cloud Connectors that are enrolled with Private Access automatically establish a secure connection to an optimal Private Access Public Service Edge or Private Service Edge in the ZTE.
This secure connection allows for the workloads accessing private applications to be securely tunneled to the Private Access Public Service Edge or Private Service Edge
allows the data path to be connected through App Connectors configured for the accessed application.

zpa-nearest.statement: Like Zscaler Client Connector, Cloud Connector tries to resolve the most optimal or nearest Private Access Public Service Edge or Private Service Edge for private application access.

quotes: Cloud Connector, similar to Zscaler Client Connector, attempts to resolve the most optimal or nearest Private Access Public Service Edge or Private Service Edge for private application access.

fail-open-egress.title: Where fail-open traffic goes, and where the fail-open toggle lives
fail-open-egress.detail: Fail-open applies only when no Cloud Connector in the group reaches any Internet & SaaS Service Edge, yet the article says fail-open egress "is flowing through Zscaler for inspection and policy control". Whether fail-open traffic goes direct to the internet uninspected or through some retained Zscaler path is not resolved; neither reading should be stated as fact. The article also does not name where the setting is changed (the gateway `failClosed` member is the likely place). The ledger entry's third question, the health-probe port, is in cloud-connector.overview.load-balancing:probe-port.
fail-open-egress.blocks: telling an operator whether workloads stay inspected during a full Service Edge outage

tertiary-control.title: Whether the tertiary Service Edge attempt is configurable
tertiary-control.detail: Unverified legacy statement: "Tertiary gateway is automatic, not user-configured. A tenant that wants full control over failover sequencing has only primary/secondary configurable." The source says the tertiary attempt happens "by default", which leaves open whether it can be disabled.
tertiary-control.blocks: answers about which Service Edges a Cloud Connector can end up using

sessions-on-failback.title: What happens to sessions on the secondary when the primary recovers
sessions-on-failback.detail: Unverified legacy statement: "Existing sessions on secondary continue until they terminate naturally. No forced migration." The source states only that new sessions go through the primary again.
sessions-on-failback.blocks: explaining long-lived connections after a failback

control-plane.title: Direction and ports of the Cloud Connector control channel
control-plane.detail: Unverified legacy statement: the control plane is "Cloud Connector's bidirectional management channel to the Zero Trust Exchange for config, heartbeat, policy updates", both planes are outbound-only, and "No inbound connection is ever made to a Cloud Connector from Zscaler's side." Other captures establish that a management plane exists and is monitored (cloud-connector.insights.connector-status:inactive-meaning; control plane health checks raise Event logs, cloud-connector.logs.event-records:when-generated), but none states its direction, ports or whether anything is ever inbound.
control-plane.blocks: firewall and security-group design for the Cloud Connector management interface

no-direct-path.title: Whether workloads and App Connectors ever connect directly
no-direct-path.detail: Unverified legacy statement: on the Private Access path (Workload, Cloud Connector, ZPA Service Edge, App Connector, application), Cloud Connectors and App Connectors "never talk directly". The high-availability article describes the path through the Service Edge but does not say a direct connection is impossible.
no-direct-path.blocks: security reviews of the workload-to-private-app path
